newsitem.title: USA: Historian gives White House lecture on Jackie O.
newsitem.headline: Historian gives White House lecture on Jackie O.

text.p: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis dreamed of writing the great American novel when she was young but wound up living it, historian Carl Anthony said Tuesday.

Anthony, the author of a new oral history about the former first lady called "As We Remember Her," sketched the life of one of America's most intriguing women at a White House lecture hosted by Hillary Rodham Clinton.

The lecture and subsequent reception on the state floor of the executive mansion reunited many of the people who served in the Kennedy administration, including speechwriter Arthur Schlesinger, Jr. and several aides to the former first lady.

After Jackie wed the man who went on to become the 35th president of the United States, she wanted to go on writing, Anthony said, but her author-politician husband told her that "one writer in the family is enough."

President John Kennedy, who wrote "Profiles in Courage" and "While England Slept", was assassinated in Dallas in 1963. His wife continued to promote the arts and historic restoration, her two favourite causes as first lady, until her death from cancer three years ago at age 64.
"Instead of writing the great American novel, she lived it," Anthony said. His book is published by Harper-Collins.

Anthony said that after Greek shipping tycoon Aristotle Onassis died, widowing Jackie for the second time, she took an entry-level editing job in a New York publishing house and called it "the happiest time of my life."

Mrs. Onassis went on to gain a certain prominence in literary circles, causing her to remark that "maybe people will now realise there was something beneath the pillbox hat," Anthony said, referring to her trademark head covering.
